data.current_description: Canonical vendor search — the resolution chokepoint. Call this FIRST to turn a vendor name/domain into a catalog vendor_id before any stack write. Answers 'who makes X?', 'find me a CRM vendor', 'what vendor is on this domain?'. An empty result is normal. AI filters (ai_capability, min_autonomy) narrow by what the software's AI concretely does and how much it does without a person. Both rest on MODEL-DETECTED, NOT-YET-VERIFIED capability data covering only the vendors we have mapped in detail — an absent vendor means unmapped, not AI-free. min_autonomy 3-4 returns empty by design: those levels assert unsupervised operation, which capability data cannot establish.
data.summary_suggestion: Resolve vendor names/domains to canonical catalog IDs
data.description_suggestion: Canonical vendor search operation that resolves vendor names, domains, or categories to catalog vendor_ids. This is the required first step before adding vendors to a stack. Supports filtering by AI capability (ai_capability parameter) and autonomy level (min_autonomy parameter). AI capability data is model-detected and covers only vendors with detailed mappings; absent vendors indicate unmapped status, not lack of AI. Note: min_autonomy levels 3-4 return empty results by design, as they require unsupervised operation which cannot be verified. Returns an array of matching vendors or empty array if no matches found.

data.current_summary: Batch-resolve messy vendor names to catalog ids
data.current_description: Batch-resolve a pasted/messy vendor list (e.g. an AP-export column) to catalog vendor_ids in one call. A READ (it never mutates state — hence NOT consequential) that takes an array body. Per submitted name returns { submitted, status, confidence, resolved_vendor_id?, resolved_name?, candidates? } where status is 'resolved' (high-confidence — use the id directly), 'ambiguous' (several close matches — show the dealer the candidates), or 'unresolved' (no confident match — do NOT invent a vendor). Resolve the whole list, THEN POST /stack/vendors per resolved row with its vendor_id + monthly_cost. Conservative on purpose: a wrong auto-match is worse than unresolved, and the no-free-text moat holds on the write side regardless.
data.description_suggestion: Batch-resolve a list of vendor names (e.g., from AP exports) to catalog vendor_ids in a single read-only operation. Accepts an array of vendor names in the request body. Returns an array of resolution objects, each containing: submitted (original name), status ('resolved', 'ambiguous', or 'unresolved'), confidence score, resolved_vendor_id (if resolved), resolved_name (if resolved), and candidates array (if ambiguous). Use resolved_vendor_id directly for 'resolved' status; present candidates to the dealer for 'ambiguous' status; do not auto-match 'unresolved' entries. After resolving, POST each resolved row to /api/v1/stack/vendors with its vendor_id and monthly_cost. This operation is intentionally conservative: incorrect matches are worse than unresolved entries.

data.current_summary: Batch-resolve messy vendor names to catalog ids
data.current_description: Batch-resolve a pasted/messy vendor list (e.g. an AP-export column) to catalog vendor_ids in one call. A READ (it never mutates state — hence NOT consequential) that takes an array body. Per submitted name returns { submitted, status, confidence, resolved_vendor_id?, resolved_name?, candidates? } where status is 'resolved' (high-confidence — use the id directly), 'ambiguous' (several close matches — show the dealer the candidates), or 'unresolved' (no confident match — do NOT invent a vendor). Resolve the whole list, THEN POST /stack/vendors per resolved row with its vendor_id + monthly_cost. Conservative on purpose: a wrong auto-match is worse than unresolved, and the no-free-text moat holds on the write side regardless.

Returns an array of resolution objects, each containing: submitted (original name), status ('resolved', 'ambiguous', or 'unresolved'), confidence score, resolved_vendor_id (if resolved), resolved_name (if resolved), and candidates array (if ambiguous). Use resolved_vendor_id directly for 'resolved' status; present candidates to the dealer for 'ambiguous' status; do not auto-match 'unresolved' entries. After resolving, POST each resolved row to /api/v1/stack/vendors with its vendor_id and monthly_cost. This operation is intentionally conservative: incorrect matches are worse than unresolved entries.
